# 12-Week Spanish Plan: Beginner to A2

A focused 5-hours-per-week plan built around travel conversations, pronunciation, and core grammar. It aims to get you speaking early, reviewing often, and tracking progress simply.

## Weekly Roadmap

| Week | Goal | Practice Activities | Progress Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Learn sounds, greetings, and self-introductions | 2 pronunciation sessions; memorize greetings; record a 30-second intro | Can say name, nationality, and basic greetings clearly |
| 2 | Build survival phrases for travel | Practice asking for help, directions, prices; shadow short audio clips | Can handle 10+ useful travel phrases without reading |
| 3 | Master present-tense basics | Learn subject pronouns and regular -ar verbs; make simple sentences | Can describe what you do daily in 5–6 sentences |
| 4 | Handle shopping and food conversations | Practice ordering food, asking for items, numbers, and quantities | Can order a meal and ask for prices confidently |
| 5 | Use questions and negation | Practice question words, yes/no questions, and “no” sentences | Can ask and answer simple questions in a dialogue |
| 6 | Talk about routines and places | Learn -er/-ir verbs; describe where you go and what you do | Can describe a typical day using present tense |
| 7 | Navigate transport and accommodation | Practice hotel check-in, transport, and time expressions | Can book a room or ask for travel details simply |
| 8 | Expand pronunciation and listening | Focus on stress, vowel clarity, and common connected speech | Can understand short slow travel dialogues better |
| 9 | Use common past tense for travel stories | Learn high-frequency preterite forms and key irregulars | Can say what you did yesterday in simple terms |
| 10 | Describe preferences and comparisons | Practice “me gusta,” “quiero,” “puedo,” and comparisons | Can explain likes, needs, and simple choices |
| 11 | Simulate real travel situations | Role-play airport, restaurant, museum, and emergency scenarios | Can complete 3-minute role-plays with less hesitation |
| 12 | Review and consolidate to A2 | Review grammar, vocabulary, and speaking; do a final mock trip | Can manage basic travel conversations end-to-end |

## Weekly Study Structure

Use the same 5-hour rhythm each week:

- **1 hour** pronunciation and listening
- **1 hour** grammar
- **1 hour** vocabulary for the week’s topic
- **1 hour** speaking practice or role-play
- **1 hour** review, flashcards, and a short self-test

## Practice Activities by Focus

### Travel Conversations
- Role-play airport check-in, hotel arrival, ordering food, and asking for directions
- Learn ready-made phrases first, then swap in new words
- Practice numbers, time, dates, and prices every week

### Pronunciation
- Shadow 1–2 minute audio clips 3 times per week
- Record yourself and compare vowel clarity, rhythm, and stress
- Focus on:
  - pure vowels
  - rolling or approximating “r”
  - clear final syllables
  - speaking in short phrase chunks

### Basic Grammar
- Start with present tense and high-frequency verbs
- Add question forms, negation, and common preterite forms later
- Keep grammar tied to speaking tasks, not isolated memorization

## Simple Progress Tracker

Use a 3-line weekly log:

- **Can say:** list 5–10 phrases or sentence patterns you can use confidently
- **Can understand:** list what you can follow in listening or reading
- **Need review:** list 3 weak points for next week

### Weekly Scorecard
Rate each item from 1 to 5:

- Pronunciation
- Travel vocabulary
- Grammar accuracy
- Listening
- Speaking confidence

Target: move each score up by at least 1 point every 2–3 weeks.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Practice Travel Phrases] https://www.memrise.com/en/learn-spanish

## Sources

- Spanish pronunciation guide: https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/spanish-pronunciation
- Spanish grammar reference: https://www.spanishdict.com/guide/spanish-grammar
- CEFR A2 overview: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/level-descriptions
